column1: Request: The Ritualist blog post break down Intention: Promote the blog and themes To be posted: October 17Story set needed: Yes - Story and feed Copy: Slide 1: Five Ways to Connect with Spirit Through Rituals of Adornment Slide 2: Perhaps you are already working with jewelry ritually subconsciously, or maybe you are already ritually minded, casting spells with your sacred and favorite pieces. Here are five ways to connect with spirit through rituals of adornment.Slide 3: 1. Wearing Jewelry to Set an Intention Call on rituals of adornment to help set intentions. To do this, first, cleanse the piece using sacred smoke, salt, or crystals. Then, hold the jewelry in both your hands. Speak your intention over the jewelry three times. Slide 4: 2. Adornment as a Protection Spell Speak a spell of protection over your rings, earrings, necklaces, and bracelets, and feel them absorb any negative energy that comes your way. Use healing smoke to cleanse your pieces, place them in a dish of salt, or allow them to sit in the light of the moon to help clear any energy from your day-to-day. Slide 5: 3. Rituals of Adornment to Ground and Center Adorning yourself with jewelry intentionally imbued with the healing power of crystals can balance, support and transform your energetic body. When you feel your energy become low, chaotic or detached, simply pause, touch the necklace you’re intentionally wearing, and take a deep breath. Slide 6: 4. Connecting with the Moon’s Magic through Jewelry Place your jewelry on a windowsill or inside a bit of silk outside to absorb the glow and energy of the moon. You might feel called to do this on a new moon phase if you wish to enchant your jewelry with the energy of new beginnings or intention setting, or on a full moon if you wish to charge your jewelry with the powers of release, wholeness, or celebration. Slide 7: 5. Wearing Jewelry as Ancestral Veneration By wearing jewelry handed down through your family, you honor those who came before you, working with your body as an altar. If you don’t have a relationship with your ancestors, or heirlooms to wear, you can purchase auspicious pieces of jewelry in the name and honor of a specific family member, or acquire jewelry that is special to you to pass down to the next generation, as you will one day be a benevolent ancestor. Slide 8: Read the full blog post here (this would just be in the story set)

column1: Slide One: What is the Shadow Self? & Why Should I Connect with It? Slide Two: Everyone has a Shadow Self. The term was popularized by psychiatrist & psychoanalyst Carl Jung, & refers to an unconscious part of a person that constitutes a blind spot or repressed traits. Perhaps you’re prone to jealousy, reactivity, or judgment. The Shadow is somehow deemed “not ideal” and therefore not integrated with the whole individual, existing just out of sight. Slide Three: Image Slide Four: Invite your demons to tea. Slide Five: Their wisdom may surprise you. Slide Six: Your Shadow Self longs to be accepted & seen. It asks you to get curious about the parts of yourself that you reject, so that you can live a more empowered and authentic life. Slide Seven: The Shadow offers wisdom and clarity. It celebrates your wholeness. Slide Eight: Honor & integrate your Shadow through ritual, journaling, meditation, practicing non-judgment, & working with a professional. Slide Nine: Your Shadow Self is full of rich wisdom, lessons, and deep self-love.

column1: Before you know what kindness really is you must lose things, feel the future dissolve in a moment like salt in a weakened broth. What you held in your hand, what you counted and carefully saved, all this must go so you know how desolate the landscape can be between the regions of kindness. How you ride and ride thinking the bus will never stop, the passengers eating maize and chicken will stare out the window forever. Before you learn the tender gravity of kindness, you must travel where the Indian in a white poncho lies dead by the side of the road. You must see how this could be you, how he too was someone who journeyed through the night with plans and the simple breath that kept him alive. Before you know kindness as the deepest thing inside, you must know sorrow as the other deepest thing. You must wake up with sorrow. You must speak to it till your voice catches the thread of all sorrows and you see the size of the cloth. Then it is only kindness that makes sense anymore, only kindness that ties your shoes and sends you out into the day to mail letters and purchase bread, only kindness that raises its head from the crowd of the world to say it is I you have been looking for, and then goes with you every where like a shadow or a friend.

column1: Caption find your sanctuaries we tend to think of a sanctuary as somewhere we have to escape to. somewhere quiet, beautiful, far enough away from everyday life that we can finally exhale. but finding sanctuary doesn’t require escape, expense, or excess. a sanctuary is a container. a space that gives you something you need in order to come back to yourself. and different sanctuaries can give us different things. a library can be a sanctuary because it gives you somewhere to feed your mind. you can find writers who make you feel less alone, ideas that open something up in you, or words that bring you new perspective. water can be a sanctuary when you need to clear your energy. your body can be a sanctuary because it is the one home you always carry with you. a place where you can belong to yourself completely. where you don’t have to perform, prove, or be anything other than who you are. your rituals can create sanctuary when they connect you to the sacred. you might have more than one sanctuary. I know I do. as you keep building your grounding practice this month, find your sanctuaries and practice returning to them. these are the spaces that bring you back - that help you feel more like yourself again. #wordsforyourjourney #gentlereminders
